pattern_temple.name: Pattern temple
pattern_temple.description: A Moorish court built from primitives - quads, boxes, cylinders, a hemisphere and a ring - in which every surface is a pattern receiver: floor, far wall, east and west walls, the entrance wall with its corbelled arch, eight columns, the dome they carry and the frieze. One desk targets a surface and dresses it through wallpaper_tile.gdshader: SOURCE (zellige, stars, lattice, khatam, brick, three rasters from the tiling halls, every package the Pattern Studio has saved under commons/patterns), GROUP (the 17 wallpaper groups), PALETTE (Alhambra, terracotta, azul, midnight), SEED, AGE (dirt, wear, dust, cracks, chips, sun fade together), ALL and CLEAN. Map-token keys: age 0-4, source, group, palette, target.
pattern_temple.qfep_connection: The same rule dresses a floor, a wall, a column and a dome differently because the receiver is a body with an orientation, a curvature and a distance from the eye; the pattern does not decide what it is on.
interactions: TARGET moves the glowing marker to the next surface: floor, far wall, east, west, entrance, columns, dome, frieze.
SOURCE, GROUP, PALETTE and SEED change what the targeted surface wears; AGE weathers it in four steps.
ALL copies the targeted surface's dressing to every surface; CLEAN removes the weathering everywhere.
The studio's Save to Godot adds a package to the SOURCE cycle on the next visit.
